newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end slightly higher in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end slightly higher in quiet trade.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed slightly higher on Sunday in quiet trading with the market expecting the central bank to leave interest rates unchanged on Monday , traders said.
Indices:
* Government bonds general: +0.06 pct to 110.17
* CPI-linked government bonds: +0.04 pct to 110.2
* Unlinked government bonds: -0.01 pct 109.92
* Dollar-linked government bonds: +0.52 pct to 110.57
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.1 pct to 108.16
Volume including Makams was an average 144 million shekels.

"The market is stable at these levels with only minor price changes both in CPI-linked and unlinked bonds," said a trader. "No one is expecting the central bank to change interest rates tomorrow," she said.

The Bank of Israel slashed its base lending rate in mid-June by 1.2 percentage points to an annualised 12.7 percent. The central bank will announce its monthly monetary programme for August on Monday.
"The market is waiting to see how two things develop: inflation and government bond issues," said Baruch Glicksberg, investment manager for a leading institutional investor.

"No one knows where inflation is going. But the market is already feeling a tight supply in bonds because bond redemptions are far higher than the new issues. The government has also agreed to further cut the budget. All this will cause yields to continue to fall lower," Glicksberg said.
Yields of CPI-linked bonds ranged between 3.85 to 4.00 percent, Ofer Dori at Ofek Securities said.

The rise of the dollar against the shekel in June, which caused June's CPI to rise a steep 1.1 percent, has triggered fears of a series of high indices. The shekel has recovered some of its losses against the dollar in the past two weeks.
The Israeli cabinet approved an 800 million shekel cut in the 1997 budget last week.

The cuts were the third round of budget slashing since the draft 1997 budget was presented last autumn. The government had earlier approved some seven billion shekels in cuts and revenue- raising measures.

"Prices of dollar-linked bonds rose today on the rise of the dollar against the shekel on Sunday," Dori said. The representative rate for the dollar on Friday was fixed at 3.5530 shekels to the dollar against 3.5220 shekels on Thursday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
($1 = 3.55 shekels)
- Shoshanna Solomon, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211
